description:
## What

Thin adapter crate wrapping `pkix-pkilint-bridge` (PKIX-jy95.8) findings as workspace `Lint` impls.

Analogous to `pkix-policy-zlint` (PKIX-jy95.10), but for pkilint (Python, DigiCert, strong on S/MIME BR + ETSI).

## Open sub-decision (granularity)

PKIX-jy95.1 decided **A2: per-check, runtime-enumerated** for zlint. The cascade note explicitly flagged: "Likely same A2 pattern for PKIX-jy95.8 (pkix-pkilint-bridge) but that's an independent decision (pkilint's lint organization differs)."

pkilint's lint organization is **module-based** (e.g., `cabf_serverauth`, `cabf_smime`, `etsi`). Each module exposes checks. Two reasonable adapter shapes:

- **(a) Per-check (mirror zlint A2):** one `Lint` per pkilint check across all modules. Probably hundreds.
- **(b) Per-module:** one `Lint` per pkilint module, where the Lint runs all checks in the module and aggregates findings.

(a) keeps parity with `pkix-policy-zlint` and matches the workspace's "one Lint = one rule" framing. (b) matches pkilint's natural shape but loses per-check granularity in workspace Finding output.

**Recommend (a) for parity** unless pkilint's per-check API is awkward to enumerate. If pkilint only exposes module-level entry points and not per-check enumeration, that forces (b).

File this as a sub-decision on PKIX-jy95.11 when implementation starts. Marking the sub-decision with `human` label so it surfaces for a decision before code lands.

## Shape (assuming per-check)

```rust
pub struct PkilintLint {
    info: PkilintLintInfo,        // from pkix_pkilint_bridge::enumerate_lints()
    bridge: Arc<PkilintBridge>,
}

impl Lint for PkilintLint {
    fn id(&self) -> &str { self.info.check_id }
    fn citation(&self) -> &str { /* from info */ }
    fn check(&self, cert: &Certificate, ctx: &LintContext) -> LintResult {
        // call bridge.run_on_cert(cert) — cached per cert
        // look up self.info.check_id in returned per-check verdicts
    }
}

pub fn all_lints(bridge: Arc<PkilintBridge>) -> Vec<Box<dyn Lint>> { /* ... */ }
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pkix-policy-pkilint` crate added to workspace
- [ ] Granularity sub-decision recorded (per-check vs per-module)
- [ ] Round-trip test against pkilint's own testdata (cite pkilint upstream)
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry
- [ ] AGENTS.md updated to mention `pkix-policy-pkilint` ships

## Out of scope

- Bridge crate implementation (PKIX-jy95.8)
- Migrating workspace S/MIME or ETSI lints to defer to pkilint (those don't exist in workspace today; pkix-lint-cabf is the small reference set)

## Blocks on

- PKIX-jy95.8 — pkix-pkilint-bridge ships first
- (a)/(b) granularity sub-decision (file as PKIX-jy95.11.1 when work begins)

## Cross-references

- PKIX-jy95 (parent, closed after .10/.11 filed)
- PKIX-jy95.1 (zlint granularity = A2 per-check; pkilint granularity is independent)
- PKIX-jy95.6 (two-layer adapter pattern)
- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5

(b) Human sub-decision: PKIX-jy95.11 description explicitly says 'File this as a sub-decision on PKIX-jy95.11 when implementation starts. Marking the sub-decision with human label so it surfaces for a decision before code lands.' The decision is per-check (mirror zlint A2, ~hundreds of Lint instances) vs per-module (pkilint's native organization with handful of module-level Lints). Both shapes have trade-offs the bead description spells out.

PKIX-jy95.10 (zlint adapter, shipped 2026-05-13 at 81026ae5) sets a per-check precedent. For parity it's natural to mirror that here; for pkilint-native ergonomics the per-module shape better matches pkilint's API. Need Mark's call before code lands.

Loop moves on. Will surface naturally after (a) PKIX-jy95.8 unblocks AND ships, and (b) granularity sub-decision is recorded.
